unresolved_questions: What is the receiver? __thiscall settles that ECX carries it and vftable_slot_dispatch settles why, but nothing settles what it is. The body reads the word, stores it in a dead frame slot and never dereferences it, and the record states bounds_only with shape null, so no type, no object size and no field offset is available from this target. Establishing it needs the class that owns one of the 199 referencing vftables - R1-VFT names 0x013ef620 slot 5 as the evidence but a slot is not a class - and not more analysis of these 13 bytes.

Which classes are folded onto this address? The derived record counts 199 sound vptr-backed vftables holding it and attributes one of them (0x013ef620, slot 5) as its receiver evidence; the remaining 198 are named by neither table nor slot here, the binary has no MSVC RTTI, and so no owning class is recoverable from this package's evidence. This is the open question the vftable_slot_dispatch rule works around rather than answers.

What is the pushed 4-byte word for? It is a data address (0x013f4ac0) at one call site and a register (EDX) at the other, and this body never reads it, so its meaning belongs to the fold group this address is part of, not to this body. Under __thiscall the word is an ordinary stack argument of an unnamed type; the callee pops it and never looks at it.

Does anything read the dead frame local? The listing shows no read inside this body, so a read can only come from outside the frame's lifetime - which no x86 code can do - or from an aliased frame this package cannot see. The store is dead in this body; whether it is a compiler artefact of a larger original statement is not observable from 13 bytes.

DEFECT, REPRODUCED AND REPAIRED. The bare-assembly probe probe_call_shape is a cdecl function, so the i386 System V rule binds it: EBX, ESI, EDI and EBP must survive the call. The probe read its fourth argument into EBX and its fifth into ESI, used EBX to push the callee's stack word and ESI to write the result word, and restored NEITHER. Two callee-saved registers were therefore destroyed in the CALLER, silently, because a caller's loop counter or pointer usually lives in one of them. The damage surfaces as an optimiser-dependent abort in a check that has nothing to do with the probe. MEASURED, on the unrepaired file: the model test exited 0 at -O0 and aborted (SIGABRT, shell status 134) at -O1, -O2 and -O3 under BOTH g++ 16.2.1 and clang++ 22.1.8 - six failing cells. An independent register-discipline probe calling the same probe with sentinels in EBX, ESI and EDI confirmed the mechanism directly: at -O2 EBX and ESI came back changed under g++ and EBX under clang++, all three preserved at -O0. So the reported defect is real and it is one register wider than first reported: EBX was clobbered as well as ESI. REPAIR, following the discipline already applied to the sibling package 0x0052e640: the probe was rewritten to touch ONLY EAX, ECX and EDX - the three caller-saved registers - plus its own %ebp/%esp, and to keep every value it needs across the call in its own 32-byte frame, reached by %ebp-relative operands. EBX, ESI and EDI are now never written. The local reservation grew from 20 to 32 bytes, the samples moved to fixed frame slots (B-4 target, B-8 out, B-12 before, B-16 argument pointer, B-20 after, B-24 eax_after) and caller_must_pop is read back straight off the frame at 16(%ebp) instead of being carried in EDX. The dead frame word is now read at -48(%ebp) rather than -16(%esp): an absolute address in this probe's own frame, so it samples the same place whether the callee popped its word or left it for the caller, which is the same reason the sibling probe reads through %ebp. NO RECONSTRUCTED SEMANTICS CHANGED: reconstruct_0052e650.cpp and reconstruct_0052e650.hpp are byte-for-byte untouched, and the entry's own transcription is unchanged. RE-VERIFIED: all eight cells exit 0; the register-discipline probe reports EBX, ESI and EDI PRESERVED at -O0, -O2 and -O3 under both compilers; and all fourteen documented mutations still die at every level under both compilers (see focused_test.mutation_verified).

(3) OFFSET - the interpreter's frame-local word moved one word further below the frame pointer (run.bp - 1 becomes run.bp - 2): the interpreter and the reconstruction disagree on where the value landed, SIGABRT under both. (4) DISCRIMINATOR THE LISTING DOES NOT HAVE - the reconstruction dereferences the receiver word: SIGSEGV under both, because the probe hands it values that are not mapped addresses. (5) CONSTANT IN THE MACHINE BYTES - the RET immediate byte in kTargetBytes changed from 0x04 to 0x08: caught at COMPILE time by the header's static_assert ("0x0052e65a is RET 0x4 (c2 04 00)") under both compilers. (6) BRANCH CONDITION - a conditional added to the store, substituting 1 for a zero receiver word: SIGABRT under both. (7) STORE - the stored word inverted rather than stored: SIGABRT under both. (8) CONSTANT - kRetImmediateBytes changed from 4 to 8: SIGABRT under both, because the modelled stack pointer stops matching the interpreter's and the cleanup comparison against the caller-cleaned twin stops matching too. (9) MACHINE BODY IN THE TEST - the mnemonic-spelled body changed to store EAX instead of ECX, so the two executed bodies no longer agree on the frame slot: SIGABRT under both. (10) THE ENTRY ITSELF - the naked entry changed to store EDX instead of ECX: SIGABRT under both, on the entry-vs-target byte check and on the frame slot the probe reads back. (11) THE ENTRY'S TERMINAL - ret $4 replaced by a plain ret: SIGABRT under both, on the entry-vs-target byte check and because the callee then leaves the caller's pushed word behind (after == before - 4). (12) THE ENTRY'S TERMINAL - ret $4 replaced by ret $8: SIGABRT under both, on the byte check and because the callee then pops a word the caller never pushed (after == before + 4). (13) THE ENTRY'S EPILOGUE - the POP EBP replaced by a read of the argument slot: SIGABRT under both, on the entry-vs-target byte check and on the argument canary, which the entry then changes. (14) THE CONVENTION - ConventionVerdict52e650 reverted to an unknown-convention enumerator: caught at COMPILE time under both compilers, because the model test pins the enumerator the derived record names. COVERAGE IS NOW EIGHT CELLS PER MUTANT, NOT TWO: the run above was a single-level -O2 run under two toolchains, and the earlier wording ('each under both g++ -m32 and clang++ -m32') understated it. The signals are unchanged and agree with the per-mutation text above - SIGABRT (-6) for the behavioural mutants, SIGSEGV (-11) for the dereference mutant, and a compile-time static_assert failure for the two constant mutants.
